text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said he expects subsidies for farmers will drop as a result of the planned eastward expansion of the European Union.

- Chief whip of the conservative People's Party Andreas Khol said government partner the Social Democrats should not allow Bank Austria and chief executive Gerhard Randa to dominate politics. A debate about German WestLB's first option on the City of Vienna's Bank Austria shares hit the share price ahead of a closed government meeting this week.
- Austria beat Latvia 3-1 in a World Cup qualifier in Riga. This win helps the team's bid to take part in the 1998 Football World Cup to be staged in France.
- The government says army purchases were worth 20.6 billion schillings to the economy between 1978 and 1996 and secured 4,000 jobs.
- Without an export offensive Austria's current account deficit will fall short of the forecast 39 billion schillings deficit this year, experts say.
- Austrian EU-Commissioner Franz Fischler said Austria should look at the Swiss model for bank accounts in order to end a row with Brussels over anonymous accounts.
- Most members of Austria's parliament favour the reduction of the blood-alcohol levels for car drivers to 0.05 percent.
- The budgets for 1998 and 1999 are at the centre of a closed meeting of the government in eastern Austria this week.
- Social Democrat chief whip Peter Kostalka wants to introduce an independent inspector of Austria's judiciary.
- Do-It-Yourself chains are rapidly expanding while sales cannot keep up with the development. Therefore competition is reducing profits.
- Insurer Wiener Staedtische and other Bank Austria shareholders are considering taking legal action against anyone harming the bank.

- Raiffeisen Bank Salzburg's chief Manfred Holztrattner says decentralised banks in Austria should jointly take over the government's stake in postal savings bank PSK, which is due to be privatised soon. He says he wants to reduce the damage of the PSK's licence to sell private loans.
